summary: Token-scoped residency mismatch causing auth handshakes and regional egress flips for multi-tenant account
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after upgrading client tokens to include per-request residency claims, some requests for a subset of tenants begin routing intermittently to eu-west edges even though account-level residency is set to us-west. Impact: Increased p50 and p95 latency (observed p95 spikes up to +700ms), multiple TLS rehandshakes and auth retries observed by the customer, and degraded SLA for large batch jobs. Environment: Production; multi-tenant account on dedicated plan; customer sends X-Redwood-Residency header derived from token claim. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer account credentials with token A (claim residency: us-west). 2) Send sustained streaming requests to /v1/chat/stream with concurrent connections from a test client that rotates tokens every 30s. 3) Observe which edge the request egresses from and measure end-to-end latency. Observed behavior: During token rotation windows the control plane sometimes selects a different egress path (eu-west) for the same tenant; requests fail transiently with TLS renegotiate or 401 auth retries and show additional hop time (~250-700ms). Expected behavior: Token-scoped residency claims should be validated against account-level residency and only permit compatible egress paths; routing should not flip mid-session due to token refresh. Temporary workaround: Customer temporarily removed per-request residency claim from tokens and reverted to account-level residency pins; latency returned to baseline. Additional context: Customer has integration that refreshes short-lived tokens every 30s. When refresh coincides with our edge affinity refresh window, routing selection logic appears to prefer the new token's residency claim over the account pin, causing a multi-hop handoff.

comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reached out reporting spikes after they started sending residency claim in tokens. They can reproduce deterministically when token rotation aligns with their client reconnect window.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Assigned for initial triage. Running service trace from customer's request IDs and edge logs.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): Found pattern where auth validation occurs after routing decision in the edge handoff path. Hypothesis: token-residency is currently considered during auth step but routing decision uses cached account pin until refresh — race condition causes flip.

Priya Kapoor (Routing): Confirmed router has two code paths: fast-path uses cached tenant_pin, slow-path re-evaluates token claims when cache miss occurs. Token rotation timing can trigger slow-path and allow the token claim to override tenant pin temporarily.
Maya Chen (Support): Customer accepted suggestion to revert to account-level pin as workaround. They've paused token residency claims in production while we investigate.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): Captured full trace and uploaded to /incidents/traces/SUP-487123-20260309.gz and created PR to add stronger validation: ensure token residency cannot override account-level pin during session handoff (link to PR).
investigation_notes: 03-10: Retrieved router decision logs for request ids supplied by customer. Observed 27 instances in 6k requests where token claim mismatch coincided with routing flip.
03-11: Reproduced in staging with client rotating tokens every 30s; confirmed increased TLS renegotiate and an extra 1-2 network hops when flip occurred.
Hypothesis: Race between edge affinity cache refresh and token validation leads to temporary acceptance of token residency override for session selection.
Action: Instrument router to log which validation branch (cached-pin vs token-eval) was used; prepared a feature-flag to force strict-account-pin precedence.
Dashboards referenced: routing/egress-path-flips, auth/retry-rate, edges/tls-handshake-duration (see confluence page).
next_steps: Deploy feature-flag in staging to enforce account-level residency precedence during in-flight session selection.
Coordinate with customer to run controlled token-rotation test during maintenance window (contact: support@globedocs.example).
If staging test passes, schedule hotfix rollout to prod with 2-hour maintenance window and post-deploy observation period of 24 hours.
Add regression test into router e2e tests that simulates token rotation during affinity refresh.
workaround: Customer removed per-request residency claim from tokens and reverted to account-level residency pin; this eliminated egress flips and latency spikes.
customer_impact_summary: Several customers under the same tenant observed transient auth retries and p95 latency spikes during token rotation windows. Batch jobs experienced timeouts in worst cases; impacted SLA for the day of 2026-03-09.
